reason: I want to secure the first specimen for the journey home, and the flight specimen locker is the natural place for it.
expectation: I expect the membrane specimen to be placed in the locker, though it may need another step to secure it for flight.

alternatives.reason: Harvesting lettuce would help take some of the garden along, but I want to place the specimen first.

effect: Placing the membrane in the flight locker completed the specimen goal; the garden remains to be taken aboard.
reaction: It is reassuring that the first specimen is coming home alongside the intact core.
reason: Harvesting the new lettuce leaves is the only available combination and should help take some of the garden along.
expectation: I expect to cut some lettuce leaves for the flight galley, though they may need another step before they are ready to take aboard.

effect: The harvest produced departure lettuce leaves, ready to take to the flight galley.
reaction: Nothing notable; the harvest worked as expected.
reason: The flight galley is the natural destination for the leaves, and this is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the leaves to be prepared or stowed for the journey, completing the garden goal.

effect: The leaves became a stowed flight meal, completing the garden goal and carrying the story through liftoff.
reaction: The handful of green and the plain falling away make a satisfying departure image.

mostWorthwhile.text: Stowing the meal was most worthwhile: the garden comes along in a tangible way, and the departure gives the chapter a sense of closure.

leastWorthwhile.text: Cutting the lettuce was straightforward but had little to discover on its own.

surprise.text: The final meal led directly into the departure sequence; I had expected it to complete the garden goal but had not anticipated liftoff in the same result.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary: the locker suited the specimen, and harvesting and stowing the leaves followed the garden goal.

continue.text: I would be curious to see how Earth receives the specimens, though this chapter's simple actions felt more like a farewell than meaningful decisions.
